articles.title: How to see when your Azure Sponsorship credit will run out
articles.excerpt: Azure Sponsorship credit doesn't end with a warning. It lasts until usage consumes the whole grant or until its end date, whichever comes first, and Azure doesn't publish the remaining balance to apps…
articles.body: Azure Sponsorship credit doesn't end with a warning. It lasts until usage consumes the whole grant or until its end date, whichever comes first, and Azure doesn't publish the remaining balance to apps. If your startup runs on it, the useful question isn't "how much is left?" but "on what day does it run out at our current rate, and is that before the end date?" Here is how to answer that by hand, and how we automated it. 1. Read the balance in the Sponsorships portal The Azure Sponsorships portal shows the balance, but only to a person who is signed in. There is no app access, so no tool (ours included) can read that number for you. Two things to keep in mind when you read it: It is a snapshot. It tells you what is left, not when it will be gone.

In heavy scenes of Dark Souls III the median went from roughly 20 to 36.7 FPS on an experimental build. Along the way I collected 5 merged and 11 open PRs against Madeira, Wine, FEX and DXMT, plus a repository of scripts, which I'm publishing now. A caveat up front: I have one phone (an iPhone Air on iOS 27.2 beta) and one tester, me, so every number below comes from that single device. The games are my own, bought legitimately. The repository contains no game files, no save editors and no copy-protection circumvention, and I won't accept any. What Madeira is Madeira runs x64 Windows programs directly on an iPhone.

articles.title: A Developer's Guide to Google Business Profile API Basics
articles.excerpt: Working with local business data programmatically has become way more interesting in the last couple of years. If you're a developer who's been asked to "fix the client's Google presence," here's what…
articles.body: Working with local business data programmatically has become way more interesting in the last couple of years. If you're a developer who's been asked to "fix the client's Google presence," here's what I've learned about the Google Business Profile API ecosystem. What the API Actually Gives You The Google Business Profile API (formerly GMB API) lets you manage locations, business hours, posts, and reviews programmatically. The authentication flow is OAuth 2.0, and you'll need a Google Cloud project with the right scopes enabled. The most common mistake I see: developers assume the API is read-only. It's not. You can create posts, update business information, and manage review responses directly from your code.

articles.title: Scrape Plus Embed Pipeline: Citable Page-Change Alerts End to End
articles.excerpt: A page-change alert is useful only when an editor can open the exact source that justified it. Short answer: what a scrape plus embed pipeline looks like end to end is five separately retryable stages…
articles.body: A page-change alert is useful only when an editor can open the exact source that justified it. Short answer: what a scrape plus embed pipeline looks like end to end is five separately retryable stages: discover pages, deduplicate canonical URLs, scrape readable text, chunk and embed it, then upsert vectors with the source URL in metadata. For a media market-research tool, I would optimize for evidence before throughput. A fast alert with no retrievable URL is an assertion. A slower alert that identifies the changed page, the old and new content hashes, and the affected chunks can be checked and corrected. That distinction determines the queue boundaries, counters, and storage schema. What does a scrape plus embed pipeline look like under failure?

articles.title: JSON-LD Structured Data Basics — How Rich Results Get Generated
articles.excerpt: You have probably seen search results that show more than a blue link and a snippet: a publish date, an author, or a breadcrumb trail of the site's hierarchy. These are called rich results, and the ra…
articles.body: You have probably seen search results that show more than a blue link and a snippet: a publish date, an author, or a breadcrumb trail of the site's hierarchy. These are called rich results, and the raw material behind them is structured data embedded in the page. This post covers JSON-LD, today's most common format: what it describes and how to verify it, using the implementation on this blog (wpmm.jp/blog and en.wpmm.jp/blog) as the example. Note: structured data is an annotation that presents a page's meaning in a machine-readable form. Writing it does not guarantee any particular display. It is a hint that helps a search engine understand the content.

articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor.
